:::{#def-irreducible-error}
#### Irreducible error

In @thm-epe-decomposition,
the term $\varpar = \Var{\noise}$ is the **irreducible error**.
It does not depend on the fitting procedure $\fitproc$,
so no choice of prediction can remove it.
The theorem concerns the single covariate value $\predvar$,
so $\varpar$ may differ from one covariate value to another:
it does not assume constant noise variance across covariate values.
For example, in @exr-epe-three-sources, $\varpar = 3$,
so every prediction there has expected squared error at least $3$.

Source: @wikipedia_bias_variance_tradeoff.
:::

::: {.remark .notes}

This expected prediction error decomposition into squared bias, variance, and irreducible error follows @james2021islr2e [Section 2.2.2].

:::
